themes_detail.label: Garbage Collection Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Missed Collection complaints spiked to 10 this week versus 2.8 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 264% surge—suggesting a sudden breakdown in sanitation service across CD 201 this week.
evidence: 10 Missed Collection complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (264% spike, z-score: 3.11)
Timing coincides with possible service disruption or staffing shortage in the past 7 days
Mott Haven/Melrose residents have repeatedly budgeted for improved sanitation—suggests chronic service issues now acute
reporting_angles: Contact DSNY to determine what caused the service disruption this week—labor shortage, equipment failure, or route change?
Interview residents about uncollected garbage piling up; identify specific blocks affected
Cross-reference with 311 data on Dirty Condition (308 complaints in 90 days) to show ripple effects

themes_detail.label: Illegal Parking & Blocked Driveways Surge
themes_detail.summary: Blocked Driveway complaints jumped 79% to 32 this week versus 17.9 weekly average over 8 weeks, signaling a sudden spike in parking enforcement or resident frustration over the past 2 weeks in this district.
evidence: 32 Blocked Driveway complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 17.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (79% spike, z-score: 3.47)
Illegal Parking is already the third-highest complaint category over 90 days (1,709 total), indicating systemic problem
Spike suggests either new illegal parking behavior or residents becoming more likely to report it
reporting_angles: Investigate whether NYPD or DOT intensified enforcement 2 weeks ago, or if a new parking problem emerged (construction, event, etc.)
Interview residents about how blocked driveways affect daily life—emergency access, delivery delays
Check if the spike correlates with any announced parking meter changes or street work in the district

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Complaints Double
themes_detail.summary: Noise - Commercial complaints more than doubled 2 weeks ago to 11 versus 4.9 weekly average over 8 weeks (126% increase, z-score: 2.71), suggesting a new bar, restaurant, or venue opened or expanded recently.
evidence: 11 Commercial Noise complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 4.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (126% spike, z-score: 2.71)
Residential Noise remains the top complaint category (1,990 over 90 days), but commercial noise is now accelerating
428 DOB permits filed recently (264 alterations)—some may be commercial venues with unmitigated noise impacts
reporting_angles: Search DOB records for recent liquor license applications, restaurant permits, or nightlife venue openings on Grand Concourse or 138th Street
Interview residents about which specific blocks or businesses are generating noise; map complaints geographically
Speak with Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) about enforcement and whether the venue(s) have adequate sound mitigation

themes_detail.label: Park Safety & Homeless Assistance Concerns
themes_detail.summary: Park Rules violations surged 2,300% three weeks ago (3 complaints vs. 0.1 baseline, z-score: 8.69) and Homeless Person Assistance jumped 269% (12 complaints vs. 3.2 baseline, z-score: 3.52), pointing to acute public safety or service gaps in district parks.
evidence: Violation of Park Rules: 3 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.1 avg over 8 weeks (2,300% spike, z-score: 8.69—highest statistical severity)
Homeless Person Assistance: 12 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 3.2 avg over 8 weeks (269% spike, z-score: 3.52)
Community Board has repeated budget requests for 'services for the homeless' and 'park, building, or access improvements' year after year—unmet need
reporting_angles: Document what specific park rule violations are occurring—aggressive behavior, illegal vending, encampments—and in which parks
Interview DHS and Parks Dept. about the homeless assistance spike; are new encampments forming or is existing population facing crisis?
Talk to residents and park users about safety concerns; determine if recent incidents (arrests, fights, medical emergencies) triggered complaints
Examine why the district repeats homeless services and park improvement budget requests—what systemic gaps exist?

themes_detail.label: Water Conservation Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Water Conservation complaints jumped 357% to 4 over the past 2 weeks versus 0.9 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 3.37), possibly indicating a water main break, leak, or DEP notification in the district.
evidence: 4 Water Conservation complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (357% spike, z-score: 3.37)
Heat/Hot Water is already the second-largest complaint category (1,789 over 90 days), suggesting existing water/heating infrastructure stress
Community Board has a recurring budget request to 'move a planned capital project into the budget' for DEP—water infrastructure may be degraded
reporting_angles: Contact NYC DEP to determine if there was a main break, boil water notice, or conservation alert issued in Mott Haven/Melrose 2 weeks ago
Cross-reference Heat/Hot Water complaints with Water Conservation complaints—do they cluster geographically?
Interview residents about whether they received emergency notifications or experienced service disruptions
